room_descriptions.text: Dust motes drift through shattered skylights. Rubble crunches underfoot. Something moved in the back.
Vault door stands open. Emergency lights paint the corridor red. The silence is worse than screaming.
Neon flickers above a bar. Music crackles from a speaker. For a moment, it almost feels normal.
Sand-scoured concrete bunker. Shell casings carpet the floor. Someone made a last stand here.
Stalactites drip irradiated water into glowing pools. Eyes watch from crevices in the rock.
Campfires ring a gutted shopping mall. Raiders have strung up trophies. The smell is indescribable.
Endless brown horizon broken by twisted highway overpasses. A hot wind carries the taste of rust.
Burned-out houses line a cul-de-sac. A swing set creaks in the breeze. Pre-war toys litter a yard.
Water treatment plant. Pipes groan and hiss. Something large splashes in the settling tanks.
Market stalls built from car hoods and street signs. Traders haggle over bullet casings and canned food.
Collapsed highway interchange. Vehicles frozen in a two-century traffic jam. Raiders nest in the overpass.
Pre-war office. Skeletons at desks. Terminal screens still glow with unread emails from the end of the world.
Generator hums in a fortified warehouse. Someone's rigged lights and a water purifier. Civilization persists.
Irradiated crater. Glass fused to sand. Geiger counter ticking like an angry clock. Don't linger.
Subway tunnel stretches into darkness. Rats scatter from your light. The tracks lead somewhere worse.
Coyote skull on a pike marks the border. Beyond: nothing moves that isn't trying to kill you.
Vault-Tec poster on the wall: 'Prepare for the Future!' The future came. It wasn't what they planned.
Casino floor. Slot machines still work. Skeletons clutch chips worth nothing to no one.
Military checkpoint. Sandbags, razor wire, and a sign: AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY. Everyone's dead.
Barn door swings open to reveal a makeshift arena. Bloodstains on the dirt. Cheering from above.
Hospital corridor. Gurneys overturned. Medical supplies scattered. Feral ghouls in patient gowns shamble past.
Church steeple rises above the fog. Inside, pews face a pulpit. Someone's carved 'ATOM' into the altar.
Trailer park at the edge of town. Some still occupied. A dog barks. A radio plays. Almost peaceful.
Red rocket station. Pumps dry for two centuries. The garage makes a decent shelter if you clear the mole rats.
Power armor bay. Frames stand empty like metal skeletons. One still has a fusion core glowing in its back.
Sewer grate leads down into ankle-deep irradiated water. Something growls in the echoing dark.
Farm plots behind sandbag walls. Mutfruit and tatos grow in grey soil. Someone's making it work.
Bridge over a toxic river. Green water flows sluggishly. A mirelurk surfaces, then submerges.
Rooftop overlooking the ruins. Sunset paints the rubble gold. For one minute, it's almost beautiful.
Boarded-up diner. Inside: preserved food, a working jukebox, and three skeletons at the counter.
Vault atrium. Two floors of rooms visible through shattered windows. Cafeteria tables overturned. Someone barricaded the stairs.
Cryogenic pods line the walls. Most occupants are bones. One pod still hums.
Vault classroom. ABCs on the chalkboard. Tiny skeletons in tiny chairs. The experiment started young.
Reactor level. Coolant leaks pool neon blue on the floor. The Geiger counter sings.
Overseer's office. Terminal still locked. The chair faces a wall of monitors showing empty rooms.
Vault garden dome. UV lamps burned out decades ago. Hydroponic trays hold only dust and dead roots.
Rec room. Pool table with three balls left. Someone scratched kill tallies into the felt.
Tunnel narrows to a crawl. Bones crunch against your elbows. The air tastes like copper.
Cavern opens into a cathedral of stone. Bioluminescent fungus paints the ceiling green. Something nests in the center.
Mine shaft propped with rotting timbers. Pickaxes rusted into the rock face. The deep end floods with every rain.
Underground river cuts through limestone. The current is fast and the water glows. Don't drink it.
Natural alcove with old sleeping bags and spent flares. Someone lived here. Claw marks on the walls suggest they stopped.
Cave mouth overlooking the valley. Wind moans through it like a dying animal. Good vantage point if nothing's home.
Barbed wire and sheet metal walls. Guard towers made from highway signs. A skull painted on the gate.
Cage fights in a parking garage. Raiders bet chems and bullets. The loser stays in the cage.
Raider throne room: a recliner on a pile of tires. Christmas lights strung from pipes. A crown made of bottlecaps.
Overpass camp. Bridges between wrecked cars. The raiders dump bodies off the edge for the dogs below.
Chop shop. Cars stripped to frames. The mechanics here strip more than cars.
Slave pen in a fenced yard. Water bowl like they're animals. Because to the raiders, they are.
Mess hall. Long tables, armed guards, and food that used to be someone's brahmin. Maybe someone's friend.
Command center. Maps pinned with faded pushpins. The battle plan was for a war that ended the world.
Armory cage. Weapons racked floor to ceiling. Most picked clean but the heavy ordinance stays locked.
Motor pool. APCs rusted to the concrete. One Vertibird looks almost flyable. Almost.
Firing range. Paper targets still hang. The silhouettes are full of holes from both sides of the apocalypse.
Watchtower above the settlement. Searchlight sweeps the perimeter. The guard waves you through.
General store. Shelves lined with scavenged goods. The shopkeeper knows your name and your credit.
Saloon with actual music. Someone plays guitar badly. Nobody cares. Cold beer is cold beer.
Town square. Children chase a dog. A woman hangs laundry. A man cleans a rifle. Normal is relative.
Gutted factory floor. Conveyor belts carry nothing. The machines remember what they made. You don't want to.
Lobby of a grand hotel. Chandelier crashed into the fountain. Feral doorman still stands at the entrance.

find_descriptions.text: Ammo box under a desk. Still sealed. Today's a good day.
Skeleton clutches a holotape and a pistol. One bullet spent.
Footlocker wedged behind rubble. Lock rusted open. Caps spill out.
First aid kit on the wall. Half empty. Half is better than none.
Toolbox hidden in a crawlspace. Someone's emergency stash, forgotten.
Safe behind a painting. Classic. The combo died with its owner.
Vending machine tips over. Nuka-Cola rolls across the floor.
Dead raider's pockets. Chems, caps, and a photo of someone they used to be.
Locked filing cabinet. Inside: pre-war documents and a pristine revolver.
Refrigerator still running on a micro-fusion cell. Food inside is... edible. Probably.
Duffle bag in a drainage pipe. Military supplies. Someone didn't make it back.
Medicine cabinet. Stimpaks and Med-X. The good stuff.
Overturned shopping cart full of junk. One man's trash, your survival.
Gun rack on the wall. One weapon left. Dusty but functional.
Cash register still has caps in it. Old habits die hard.
Buried in rubble: a lunchbox. Inside: bottlecaps and a toy car. Jackpot.
Chem lab equipment. Someone was cooking. Product's still here.
Power armor frame in a locked cage. The key's got to be somewhere.
Dog tags and a wedding ring. You pocket the caps, leave the rest.
Trunk of a pre-war car. Spare tire, jack, and three bottles of perfectly preserved whiskey.
Holotape wedged in a terminal. Someone's last words. You listen anyway.
Workbench with scattered components. Enough to mod a weapon if you're clever.
Child's backpack behind a dumpster. Preserved food and a teddy bear inside. You take the food.
Military crate stamped CLASSIFIED. The lock's been shot off. Mini nukes inside.
Booby-trapped door. You spot the tripwire. Whoever set it left good stuff on the other side.
Pre-war suitcase. Clothes turned to dust but the jewelry survived. Caps equivalent right there.
Bathroom mirror. Behind it: three stimpaks taped to the wall. Old survival trick.
Deathclaw nest. Eggs the size of footballs. Worth a fortune if you can carry them out alive.
Pipe rifle propped against a wall. Owner slumped beside it. Plenty of ammo left.
Nuka-Cherry in a cooler of ice that melted two centuries ago. Still cold somehow. Don't question it.
Robot vendor powered down in an alcove. Boot it up and it wants to sell you things. With what money?
Under a collapsed shelf: fusion cells. Dozen of them. Laser weapon just became viable.
Mattress in a closet. Supplies stacked neatly. Whoever lived here was organized. And gone.
Steamer trunk in the basement. Three locks. Inside: pre-war money and a plasma pistol.
Lucky find: purified water in sealed containers. Someone was hoarding for a rainy day that never came.
Flipped brahmin cart. Salvage scattered across the road. Caravan didn't make it. You will.
Burned journal. Most pages ash. One readable entry: coordinates to a cache. Could be real.
Skeleton in power armor. The armor still works. The previous owner doesn't need it.
Nuka-Cola Quantum glowing in a display case. Blue light fills the room. Beautiful and irradiated.
Surgical tray. Clean tools. Stimpak components. Someone was a doctor here once.
Grenade bouquet hanging from a doorknob. Trip it and the whole room goes. Disarm it and they're yours.
Pre-war comic book in mint condition. Worth more than caps to the right buyer. Worth nothing to your stomach.
Crate of Sunset Sarsaparilla. Still fizzy. Still terrible. Still better than irradiated puddle water.
Lockbox chained to a pipe. Inside: someone's life savings. Forty-seven caps and a silver locket.
Missile launcher under a tarp. Five missiles beside it. Merry Christmas.
Caravan manifest and a key. The cache location is circled on a map pinned to the wall.
Ghoul's bindle. Irradiated food you can't eat and caps you absolutely can spend.
Water chip. Cracked but maybe repairable. Worth its weight in gold to the right vault.
Brotherhood holotag on a dead paladin. The laser rifle beside them works fine.
Bottlecap mine in a box. Homemade explosive. Crude but effective. The caps are the shrapnel.

ambient_descriptions.text: Wind whistles through broken windows. Glass tinkles somewhere above.
Distant gunfire. Three shots, then silence. Someone won or lost.
A brahmin lows somewhere in the fog. Caravan must be close.
Geiger counter clicks steadily. Not dangerous yet. Yet.
Radio static gives way to a song. Civilization. Maybe nearby.
Crows circle overhead. They always know where the bodies are.
Thunder rolls across the wasteland. Green lightning. Rad storm incoming.
Somewhere a protectron announces: 'PROTECT AND SERVE.' Then silence.
Campfire smoke rises from behind a hill. Could be friendly. Could be anything.
A vertibird roars overhead. Brotherhood. They don't stop for wastelanders.
Dogs howling in the distance. Pack hunters. Moving away, thankfully.
Stars visible through the haze tonight. Millions of them. The sky didn't die.
Pipes groan in the walls. Something's still pressurized down here.
Smell of cooking meat drifts from a settlement. Your stomach reminds you it exists.
A muffled explosion. Then another. Someone found a mine field the hard way.
Eyebot floats past playing patriotic music. Propaganda from a dead government.
Leaves rustle. No wind. Something's watching from the treeline.
Rain patters on corrugated tin. Clean enough to drink, if you're desperate.
The creak of a door swinging open by itself. Building settling. Probably.
Footsteps echoing that aren't yours. You stop. They stop. You walk faster.
Dust devil spins across the highway. Picks up papers two hundred years old and scatters them again.
A child laughs somewhere. Then you remember there are no children here.
Mr. Handy buzzes past trimming dead hedges. Still on its schedule. The house is gone.
Radiation warning siren. Still functional. Nobody left to warn.
Moonlight through broken ceiling tiles. Your shadow stretches long and wrong.
Deathclaw roar in the distance. Far enough. For now.
Water dripping. Steady rhythm. Almost peaceful if you forget what's in the water.
Old billboard: NUKA-COLA - TASTE THE FUTURE. Bullet holes through every letter.
Caravan brahmin dead on the road. Picked clean. Flies have what's left.
Sunset through atomic haze. Orange and purple. Poisonous and gorgeous.
Howling from the metro tunnels below. Could be wind. Could be ghouls. Same difference.
A light blinks on and off in an empty building. Morse code or short circuit. You don't check.
Radstag herd crosses the road ahead. Cautious. Two-headed. Almost majestic.
The smell hits before you see the bodies. Raiders made an example. Message received.
Train whistle? No. Wind through a collapsed overpass. Sounds just like one though.
Super mutant shouting echoes between buildings. Can't tell how far. Sound plays tricks in the ruins.
Fireflies. Actual fireflies. Radioactive, but still beautiful hovering over the swamp.
Flag still flies over a government building. Tattered. Faded. Defiant.
Pre-war car alarm going off. Two hundred years and the battery won't die. Nobody's coming.
Cazador wings buzzing. That sound means run. Don't look. Just run.
Smoke column on the horizon. Settlement or raid. Hard to tell the difference sometimes.
Your Pip-Boy ticks faster. Background radiation rising. Turn around or push through.
Abandoned campfire. Still warm. Someone left in a hurry. You should too.
Gecko chirping in the rocks. Harmless ones. The harmless kind are almost cute.
Sprinkler system activates in a dead garden. Water's brown but the mechanism works. Pre-war engineering.
Blood trail leading into the dark. Fresh. You've got a choice to make.
Diamond City radio fades in. Travis stumbles through a sentence. Somehow comforting.
Two skeletons on a bench. Holding hands. Two centuries and still together.
Mirelurk eggs along the riverbank. Dozens. Stay off the shore.
Night falls fast out here. The wasteland is honest about its darkness.

npc_lines.text: War. War never changes.
Patrolling the Mojave almost makes you wish for a nuclear winter.
I don't want to set the world on fire. I just want to start a flame in your heart.
Nobody's dick is that long. Not even Long Dick Johnson.
What in the goddamn...?
Degenerates like you belong on a cross.
Another settlement needs your help.
Ad victoriam, brother.
Ain't that a kick in the head.
I survived because the fire inside burned brighter than the fire around me.
Don't feed the yao guai. That is all.
Got something different for ya this time. Caps. Sweet, sweet caps.
I'm your friend. Trust me. Would a synth say that?
When I got this assignment I was hoping there'd be more gambling.
Tunnel Snakes rule!
Two-hundred years and the vending machines still work. But not the toilets.
Wasteland survival tip: if it glows, don't eat it. If it growls, don't pet it.
The NCR has its share of problems but I like to think we're doing some good.
Atom blesses those who embrace his glow.
Keep your eyes open. Ears too. Hell, keep everything open out here.
They asked me how well I understood theoretical physics. I said theoretical.
You're not a ghoul, are you? Nah. Ghouls smell better.
In a hundred years, nobody's gonna care about any of this. That's the secret.
I'm done being afraid. The wasteland doesn't care if you're scared.
Stimpak? That'll be fifty caps. Or a story. Stories are worth more.
Seen a deathclaw once. Once was enough. I ran for three miles straight.
The Brotherhood wants technology. The Institute makes it. We just try to survive it.
Best sunset I ever saw was from the top of Tenpenny Tower. Worth the climb.
Old World Blues. That's what they call it. Missing what killed us.
